editorial_thesis: Today’s practical signal is control at the boundary: persistent compute needs explicit capacity policy, design generation needs budgets and hierarchy, and agents need identities that can be monitored and remediated.

topic_groups.title: Persistent Agent Compute
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Fresh AWS general availability adds a materially new runtime option for long-running, GPU, shared-state, and multi-agent workloads; this is a clear gap after recent coverage focused on short-lived runtimes.

sources.title: AgentCore runtime instances are now generally available
sources.why_selected: AWS made EC2-backed AgentCore runtime instances generally available.
sources.usefulness: Gives Buildn a concrete pattern for separating cheap orchestration from durable workers.

sources.title: Runtime instances: persistent compute for production AI agents
sources.why_selected: The primary architecture post explains shared sessions, files, GPUs, and hybrid runtimes.
sources.usefulness: Provides a directly testable multi-agent artifact handoff pattern.

topic_groups.title: Design System Controls
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Figma has fresh August controls for per-user AI credits and nested access-inheriting folders, plus recent annotation and CSS-aligned layout changes; this fills a product/design operations gap.

sources.title: Figma product news and release notes
sources.why_selected: The release notes contain the current AI credit and folder changes.
sources.usefulness: Maps directly to Buildn/client budgets, artifact hierarchy, and design-to-code handoff.

sources.title: Code, craft, and the making of nested folders
sources.why_selected: Figma documents the rationale behind nested folders and inherited sharing.
sources.usefulness: Offers a practical information-architecture model for client workspaces.

sources.title: Properties panel and annotations now in Figma Make
sources.why_selected: The editing and annotation surface turns visual feedback into a more precise workflow.
sources.usefulness: Can improve visual QA and agent-directed iteration.

topic_groups.title: Agent Identity + Posture
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Current Microsoft and Okta updates make agents visible to security and identity systems; this is a practical governance lane with direct client applicability and limited recent coverage overlap.

sources.title: Microsoft Defender Monthly News — August 2026
sources.why_selected: Defender adds public-preview posture-risk assessment and GA tenant-agent protection capabilities.
sources.usefulness: Provides a concrete model for agent inventory and remediation queues.

sources.title: Okta Identity Engine API release notes 2026
sources.why_selected: Okta’s August release explicitly supports AI agents as workload principals.
sources.usefulness: Supports durable ownership, audit, and revocation for delegated workflows.

sources.title: Least privilege for AI agents: Identity, access, and tool binding
sources.why_selected: The guidance names tool binding as a key least-privilege control.
sources.usefulness: Translates security principles into a Buildn tool manifest.
